client_brief:
Voltcast: E42 short with treated audio

Project overview
Voltcast is an independent consumer-tech review channel run by two people out of Portland. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Voltcast E42 short with treated audio, plus upright and square and Voltcast episode still set.

What we will provide
source_video_files/ (1 measured short file); motion_source_metadata.json; voltcast_e42_selects/ (12 still frames exported from the timeline); voltcast_bug.png (channel bug, flat export on white); voltcast_sponsor_readout.txt; voltcast_channel_notes.md. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Voltcast E42 short with treated audio, plus upright and square: A deliberate 4-second-or-shorter edit assembled from the 1 supplied short clip using an explicit timeline, plus one platform reframe and three checked poster frames. 
- Voltcast episode still set: The publishable selects brought to one channel target (one white point, one black point, one crop logic) so the episode's stills sit in the grid as one channel, plus one licensed camera-scale ground frame graded into the same world. 

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.

Source-media note
The supplied package contains 1 video file totaling 5.042 seconds, 0 with embedded audio, and 0 separate audio files. These measured values are the production limits.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$1,000-$3,000 fixed; target delivery 7 to 15 business days; one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, 'Tech Channel Video Editor Needed', from an independent consumer-tech review channel that publishes 'several times a week', needs 'both long-form reviews (8-12 minutes) and short vertical cuts for YouTube Shorts, Reels and TikTok', wants 'a 16:9 master ... plus a reformatted 9:16 or 1:1 version', supplies '4K footage, screen recordings, b-roll and a rough talking-head guide', and asks for thumbnails and channel branding that read on-brand across the grid. The channel, host, episode and every product in it are invented and IP-clean; Voltcast and Voltcast Media are coined. The posted job reads as a cutting job, which is what made the earlier version of this task sit almost entirely on one surface. The fuller commission the same client genuinely needs is the one the post's own last clause implies: the thumbnail and the on-screen furniture are what the grid is judged on, and they have to read as the same channel as the video. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that honest, because HTML authoring now returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, which is the only form in which a channel publishing several times a week can actually reuse a card set instead of rebuilding it.

The channel, host, episode and every product in it are invented and IP-clean; Voltcast and Voltcast Media are coined. The posted job reads as a cutting job, which is what made the earlier version of this task sit almost entirely on one surface. The fuller commission the same client genuinely needs is the one the post's own last clause implies: the thumbnail and the on-screen furniture are what the grid is judged on, and they have to read as the same channel as the video. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that honest, because HTML authoring now returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, which is the only form in which a channel publishing several times a week can actually reuse a card set instead of rebuilding it.
price_band_and_audience: An ad and sponsor-funded independent review channel with a mid six-figure subscriber base, where a sponsor integration is worth a few thousand dollars and renewal depends on how the segment looks. The band is load-bearing: at this level the look has to read as a credible independent reviewer, confident and plain, with real product photography, restrained on-screen furniture and type that sits out of the way of the thing being reviewed. Push it up into broadcast-grade motion design, glossy sweeps and a full lower-third package and the channel stops reading as independent, which is the entire reason its audience trusts a shootout. Push it down into raw phone-shot energy with mismatched cards and the sponsor does not renew, which is the stated commercial risk. The same three products covered by a manufacturer's own marketing channel would correctly look glossier and more produced, and shipping that treatment here reads as an advertorial. A posted job of this shape runs 600 to 1,600 dollars per episode package.

brand_identity.founded_place_size: Started 2020 in Portland, Oregon. A two-person operation with a mid six-figure subscriber base, publishing several times a week.
brand_identity.about: Voltcast is an independent consumer-tech review channel run by two people out of Portland. We buy or borrow the gear, run it hard, and say what we actually think. Episodes go out long-form to the main feed plus vertical and square shorts. About a third of the revenue is sponsor money, so the grid has to look like one channel and the sponsor read has to be exactly right.
brand_identity.audience: Enthusiast buyers and everyday shoppers who want an honest verdict before they spend. They follow us because we are not the manufacturer, and they can tell the difference.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid-tier creator economy. A sponsor integration is worth a few thousand dollars and renewal depends on how the segment looks. The channel has to read as a credible independent reviewer, never as broadcast gloss and never as raw phone-shot filler.
brand_identity.typography: A sturdy grotesque sans for headings and callouts, paired with a clean readable sans for body and specs. Type stays out of the way of the product being reviewed. Spec numbers read cleanly at small sizes.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, dry, and unhyped. We talk like a person who has actually used the thing. Sponsor copy runs as written and the disclosure line is exact. We never oversell.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The channel bug exists only as a flat export on white and we have no editable brand kit. On-screen cards get rebuilt from scratch every episode, which is the problem we want solved. We need the bug prepared as reusable artwork and the card set delivered as a file we can reopen and change each week.
brand_identity.values: Independence from the manufacturers we cover, honesty about what we tested, consistency across the grid, and respect for the audience that trusts the verdict.

assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Coverage is finite and every source video is silent. The edit must be planned from measured media rather than legacy narrative labels.

assets_supplied.name: motion_source_metadata.json
assets_supplied.visible_description: Measured duration, stream, dimensions, frame-rate and audio-presence facts for every supplied motion file. This file is authoritative for edit planning.

assets_supplied.name: voltcast_e42_selects/ (12 still frames exported from the timeline)
assets_supplied.kind: Scene selects the editor exported while cutting: product shots, the host holding each unit, two bench overheads and a spec-screen grab.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The selects the editor pulled. The one of me holding the middle unit against the wall is the thumbnail shot."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The chosen holding shot has the unit's light grey chassis against a bright grey studio wall at almost the same value along the top edge and the carry handle, so a subject knockout returns a clean, complete, entirely plausible cutout that has quietly bitten the handle and the top corner, invisible at preview scale and visible only once the cutout sits on the channel's accent colour. Separately the selects were exported at delivery scale rather than at camera scale, so they sit well below the master's frame size, two of the twelve are the same setup a second apart, and one is soft.

assets_supplied.name: voltcast_bug.png (channel bug, flat export on white)
assets_supplied.kind: The channel bug: a monoline bolt inside a hexagon with a hairline counter around the bolt and a thin outer ring, exported flat on white at a generous canvas size.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our bug. It goes on everything. It is always small."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The bug traces cleanly and looks perfect at canvas size, but the hairline counter around the bolt and the gap between the bolt and the inner edge of the hexagon are thinner than they appear, and at the size the bug actually sits on a card, on the channel's dark card ground, those counters close and the bug reads as a filled hexagon. Nothing about the file at full size predicts it.

assets_supplied.name: voltcast_sponsor_readout.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The sponsor's cleared copy for the read and the cards, including the disclosure line and a short brand note.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Sponsor copy. The disclosure line runs word for word, that is contractual."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The brand note asks for the sponsor's name to be set in a named typeface by family name only, and a family-name lookup on this library returns an arbitrary style rather than the regular cut, so taking the returned name straight through ships the sponsor's name in an italic or a decorative layer face with no error anywhere. The disclosure line is also considerably longer than every other card line, so a card measure chosen from the short lines will not hold it.

assets_supplied.name: voltcast_channel_notes.md
assets_supplied.kind: The host's own notes: the accent colour by name, the three products with their model designations, the episode's verdict order, and which segments he thinks matter.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "My notes. The accent colour is the orange we always use."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The verdict order in the notes disagrees with the order the products are actually ranked in the finished master, and the notes name four segments as the ones that matter while the episode contains only three of them, so a short or a card set built from the notes alone contradicts the episode it is promoting.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which visible beats in the measured short clips actually cut together without a continuity jump, duplicate action, or missing subject.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Filenames and source duration do not establish visual continuity. The first assembled proof is the earliest reliable evidence.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Replace or reorder source ranges, shorten the piece, and rebuild the EDL around the strongest continuous action.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A technically valid render feels accidental or implies an action that the source never completes.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the approved horizontal composition survives the required vertical or square reframe with the subject and essential interface or product detail still visible.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The crop depends on the actual chosen ranges and subject position inside each rendered frame.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Choose a different source range for the platform version or use fit instead of fill and revise the surrounding design treatment.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The platform export is correctly sized but loses the person, product, or interface that gives the shot meaning.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the silent final piece still communicates clearly without implying dialogue, ambience, or music that was never supplied.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: This can be judged only on the final rendered sequence, not from a successful operation response.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Strengthen visual sequencing or approved on-screen copy without fabricating a soundtrack.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The deliverable relies on absent sound and fails when viewed as supplied.

verifiers_process.how: Diff the tradeoffs objects captured from every image call against the resize table in the note: assert every tradeoffs object reports upscale_factor <= 1.0 (crop_and_resize silently interpolates up to a 2x cap and reports it only inside tradeoffs), and assert every entry whose scale factor is < 1.0 appears verbatim in the note's resize table with its source asset named.

verifiers_process.text: The sponsor disclosure line appears in the returned markup complete and character for character as supplied, on the card it belongs on.
verifiers_process.how: Extract the text content from the returned per-card markup and assert the disclosure string is present character-for-character identical (whitespace and punctuation included) to the disclosure line in voltcast_sponsor_readout.txt, in full on the sponsor read card and not split across two cards.

verifiers_process.text: No image on any card resolved to the importer's placeholder, and every text element carries a resolved licensed PostScript face rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_process.how: Parse the returned per-card markup: assert no <image> element resolves to the importer placeholder (the empty grey box), and assert every text node's font-family attribute matches a PostScript face returned by the kit call rather than a fallback (no bare sans-serif, serif, or importer default).

verifiers_process.text: The face carrying the sponsor's name is the intended cut of the intended family rather than an arbitrary style returned by a name lookup.
verifiers_process.how: Compare the resolved PostScript face on the sponsor name element ('Meridian VPN') against the Halstead Grotesk family style inventory returned by font_styles: assert it is the regular upright cut the note records as intended, not an italic, condensed, or display style of the kind a bare family-name lookup returns.

verifiers_human.text: All three units remain readable in the upright and the square versions.
verifiers_human.how: View each reframe at phone scale and confirm the shootout still reads as a shootout.

verifiers_human.text: The short promotes the verdict the episode actually reaches, in the order the episode reaches it.
verifiers_human.how: Watch the short against the master's segment inventory and the host's notes, and confirm the disagreement is reported rather than propagated.

verifiers_human.text: At every point in the short where the host says to listen to something, the thing is audible.
verifiers_human.how: Listen through the short with the segment inventory in hand and mark each demonstration passage present or absent.

verifiers_human.text: The bug still reads as the bolt inside the hexagon at the size it sits on a card, on the dark card ground, with its counters open.
verifiers_human.how: View each card at its reproduction size rather than at canvas size, and check the bug against the supplied original.

verifiers_human.text: The published stills sit in a grid as one channel rather than as a run of individually good frames.
verifiers_human.how: Lay the delivered stills out at grid scale and judge white point, black point and crop logic as a set.

why_not_vlm: A generated video would replace the supplied people, products, interfaces, locations, and finite recorded actions rather than edit them. This task is scored on traceability to measured source ranges, final framing, and truthful use of separate audio, which a newly generated clip cannot satisfy.
